brief.headline: Push for ₹28.69 L/yr price cut to match Mars Plastics and Premier Plastic — we're 47.43% of their sales, so we have the weight

priceAsk.summary: Cut prices on the three big SKUs to match our best suppliers — Mars Plastics and Premier Plastic
priceAsk.target: ₹28.69 L/yr total saving; PP cap from ₹1.08 to ₹0.81 (Mars price), HDPE bottle from ₹1.53 to ₹1.38 (Mars), measuring cup from ₹0.46 to ₹0.35 (Premier)
priceAsk.basis: We already pay those prices to Mars and Premier for the same items. Market research shows the 28 mm PP cap asking price is ₹0.85–0.95/pc typical, with room down to ₹0.65–0.80 at volume — so ₹0.81 is fair and in the market band.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 45 days to 30 days after receipt
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: ₹16.02 L cash freed up for us

brief.financialLeverage: They're small — ₹4.11 Cr in sales — and we're huge to them: our ₹1.95 Cr is 47.43% of everything they sell. They keep only 6.0% profit on each sale, half what similar firms keep (15.0%), so they feel price cuts hard. They owe 1.13× their own cash, which tightens things, but they pay suppliers in 39 days versus 23 days at peer firms, so they're used to managing tight cash. Bottom line: we're their biggest customer by far, so we can push firmly on price and terms — but keep the ask realistic because their margins are thin.

evidence.point: We are nearly half their business
They keep much less profit than rivals
They already stretch payment to their own suppliers longer than most
PP cap — we pay ₹1.08, Mars charges ₹0.81, gap is 33.2%, costs us ₹14.05 L/yr extra
HDPE bottle — we pay ₹1.53, Mars charges ₹1.38, gap is 10.7%, costs us ₹7.88 L/yr extra
Measuring cup — we pay ₹0.46, Premier charges ₹0.35, gap is 30.6%, costs us ₹6.75 L/yr extra

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr) — pharma bottles, caps, preforms; health score B (65/100); top second-source fit

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹946.50 Cr); pails, containers, pharma; health score B (73/100); strong, profitable alternate for bottles and closures

risks: They're in the grey zone on financial distress (Altman Z 1.83) — push firmly but don't squeeze so hard you tip them over; keep supply security front of mind
Small supplier (₹4.11 Cr, flagged as <₹10 Cr entity) and we're 47.43% of their book — if they stumble, our supply stumbles; line up Manjushree or Mold-Tek now
Their profit is half the peer level (6.0% vs 15.0%) — big price cuts may force them to walk or cut quality; tie the ask to volume commitment or longer contract to make it work for them
They carry debt at 1.13× their own cash and burned ₹79.14 L free cash last year — offer faster payment (15 days earlier frees ₹8.01 L for us) in return for the price cut to help their cash and ours
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, but we're paying ₹28.69 lakh more than our best prices on the same items — let's close that gap and talk about how faster payment can help both of us.
